detail.longDescription: I’m switching my HTML helpers from f-strings to t-strings so user input gets escaped automatically. Escaping works, but number formatting is gone. When I put one template inside another, the inner template comes out as an escaped object dump instead of HTML. from string.templatelib import Template, Interpolation import html def render(template: Template) -> str: parts = [] for item in template: if isinstance(item, Interpolation): parts.append(html.escape(str(item.value))) else: parts.append(item) return "".join(parts) name = "Rahum" price = 19.999 row = t"{name}${price:.2f}" page = t"{row}" print(render(row)) print(render(page)) What I expected: Rahum$20.00 Rahum$20.00 What happened instead (Python 3.14.6): Rahum$19.999 Template(strings=('', '$', ''), interpolations=(Interpolation('Rahum', 'name', None, ''), Interpolation(19.999, 'price', None, '.2f'))) Questions: Why is :.2f ignored? With an f-string, the same code prints $20.00 . Why does the nested row template turn into a Template(...) repr instead of rendering? How should render handle format specs, !r / !s conversions, and nested templates without double-escaping the inner HTML? Related question: This answer about t-string logging shows how to apply conversions and format specifications, but does not address nested HTML templates or double escaping.
